findings.detail: MUC5B inhibits mucociliary clearance (neg), and mucociliary clearance leads_to IPF (pos), so the arm composes to MUC5B lowering IPF risk; this is the opposite of the run's own mechanism ('mucociliary impairment ... creating a combined profibrotic environment'), so the flip sits in step 4's sign.

The run cites PMID:42532628 only under the TERT hypothesis, but its title, 'Telomere dysfunction and mucociliary impairment drive idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis susceptibility', states the opposite of step 4's sign. Under guide v2 it is now attached to step 4 as refuting evidence (moved_from hyp_tert_telomeres.3).

PMID:42532628, cited by this run, reports enrichment of MUC5B loss-of-function variants in IPF cases (OR=443.1), which sits badly with a MUC5B-overexpression mechanism; every hypothesis lists contradicting_evidence as empty, so the re-fetch had no contradicting citations to add.

No text cited for the MUC5B arm mentions mucociliary clearance; the only text in the run that does (PMID:42532628, cited under TERT) states the opposite of step 4, so the only H1 arm has no supporting evidence.

Step 1 is 'MUC5B gene increases_amount MUC5B protein', a self-loop. The re-fetched PMID:21506741 states the step the note means ('The variant allele of rs35705950 was associated with up-regulation in MUC5B expression in the lung in unaffected subjects', 37.4-fold), but the chain never puts the variant at its start, so that evidence has no step to support and no arm can start at the variant.

Mucociliary clearance is placed in alveolar type 2 cells. GO:0120197 defines it as moving mucus out of the airways by motile cilia, and CL:0002063 defines AT2 as an alveolar cell covered by microvilli.

The TOLLIP -> immune response step neither follows step 2 nor leads to step 4, so the 'TOLLIP modulates immune responses' half of the title has no route to IPF; its only gene-level link is a text-mining-only STRING edge and an IPF variant whose closest gene is MUC5B.

The CELLxGENE records behind 'upregulated in IPF' and 'loss of DSP occurs in IPF' compare pulmonary fibrosis (MONDO:0002771) or interstitial lung disease (MONDO:0015925) donors with normal donors, not IPF, and DSP's is in ciliated cells, not the alveolar epithelium named in the step.

The only paper behind the SFTPC hypothesis models the toxic gain-of-function variant SFTPC-I73T; the chain names only 'SFTPC', so the gene-to-accumulation step has no direction (now an unsigned assoc with its paper excluded as not_this_entity) and the SFTPC claim has no route.
The only text for 'AT2 dysfunction leads_to IPF' says AT2 dysfunction is key to pulmonary fibrosis in general, in a paper modelling familial pulmonary fibrosis, not IPF.
The FAM13A step sits between the Wnt -> ECM and ECM -> IPF steps but connects to neither, so the FAM13A half of the title ('FAM13A upregulation drives ... ECM remodeling') has no route.

PMID:42083809 shows the FAM13A long isoform is needed for lung epithelial lineages to emerge in iPSC development (a COPD gene); it says nothing about upregulated FAM13A driving 'aberrant epithelial states' or about IPF.
PMID:42083809 says FAM13A acts 'through dysregulating Wnt/β-catenin signaling', a link to the DSP arm the run did not draw; it has no direction, so no bridge was added.

The proposed falsification (overexpress DSP, expect ECM remodelling suppressed) is the experiment already reported in the cited PMID:42690534 ('DSP overexpression suppressed Wnt/β-catenin signaling and fibrotic gene expression'), in A549 cells.
The cited text calls aberrant ECM remodelling a characteristic of IPF; the step turns that hallmark into a cause ('leads_to IPF').

'Telomere maintenance leads_to (+) cellular senescence' contradicts the run's own mechanism ('a failure in telomere maintenance ... triggers premature cellular senescence') and its falsification (activate TERT, expect senescence averted). If step 1 were read as the note does (TERT supports telomere maintenance), the arm would compose to TERT raising IPF risk, opposite to the 'TERT deficiency' claim.
The only paper cited for the TERT hypothesis never names TERT or senescence; no TERT step has kept evidence.

Hypothesis-level supporting evidence CXG:ENSG00000164362:CL_0000861 (cited at no step) shows TERT is essentially undetected in elicited macrophages in both groups (0 vs 0.003%); it states no step of the run and has nothing to do with senescence in lung progenitors.
All four hypotheses are marked support 'grounded', yet no step into IPF has a citation that supports it (the one kept for the MUC5B arm refutes it); confidence 'low' is fair.
The run calls 'cellular senescence' a phenotype (GO:0090398 is a process) and 'endosomal accumulation' a process (it is SFTPC's amount in a compartment, curated as SFTPC refined to the endosome).

Five cited GWAS records give variant -> IPF associations with allele and effect (rs35705950-T OR 5.06; rs2076295-G OR 1.49; rs2609259-A OR 1.3; rs776981958-C beta 6.76 'unit (increase)'; rs2736100-A OR 2.11), but the run cites them for gene -> process steps they cannot state and never makes a variant step, so none can be used.

The refuting PMID:42532628 says mucociliary impairment 'drive[s]' IPF susceptibility, but its design is a rare-variant burden test in 123 cases, which its own conclusion words as 'suggests a possible role'; kept as observational, not mechanistic.

Fixed in the v2 re-fetch: v1's sources.py plain() and render.py fold() stripped '<[^>]+>', deleting 'P<0.001' up to the next tag, so PMID:21506741 lacked 'The variant allele of rs35705950 was associated with up-regulation in MUC5B expression ...'; the sentence is now present and quotable (render.py TAG now needs a letter after '<').

No form for 'protein X accumulates in compartment C' as a step from X: the step is rendered as an unsigned assoc of SFTPC with the amount of its own endosomal refinement, a stand-in that relates a node to a refinement of itself.
No GO term for 'extracellular matrix remodeling'; grounded to its parent GO:0030198 extracellular matrix organization (assembly, arrangement or disassembly).
No term for 'AT2 cell dysfunction'; curated as HP:0011017 Abnormal cellular physiology refined to CL:0002063.

Fixed since v1: a cellType context on a phenotype rendered as 'part of' (BFO:0000050), making 'AT2 cell dysfunction' 'Abnormal cellular physiology part of AT2 cell'; Ctx.cellRel now uses 'characteristic of' for phenotypes, and the v2 render shows it.

No form for 'disease has feature X' (IPF characterized by aberrant ECM remodelling): guide v2 now names the exclusion (disease_feature), but a hallmark cited as a cause can still only be excluded, not stated as what it is.

v1: the guide said an unsigned step signed from a cited text has 'observational' evidence, but here the sign comes from an in vitro knockout. Settled by guide v2 (evidence kind is the design behind the quoted span): inVitro.

Guide v2 makes every associated_with step an assoc, discounted by four fifths through fromAssoc because 'association is not causation', but this step's direction comes from a knockout (an iPSC perturbation), so the discount penalises causal evidence for the run's choice of relation word.

CXG:ENSG00000168484:CL_0002063:MONDO_0002771, cited for 'SFTPC accumulates in the endosomes of AT2 cells', says only that SFTPC is detected in 94.3% vs 92.6% of AT2 cells from pulmonary fibrosis (not IPF) vs normal donors: no endosomes, and almost no difference.

No form for gene expression ('MUC5B gene increases_amount MUC5B protein'): the guide grounds gene and protein to one UniProt node and names no checked gene CURIE, so the step is a self-loop and can only be unexpressed.

Guide v2 adds the parent_disease exclusion, so 'AT2 dysfunction is key to ... pulmonary fibrosis' is excluded for an IPF step, but BioLean has no rule carrying evidence from the parent disease (MONDO:0002771) to the subtype (MONDO:0800504) with a discount, although IPF is a pulmonary fibrosis.

The run's flipped step 4 (mucociliary clearance →+ IPF) now carries the only text that bears on it, as refutes, giving the statement disbelief 1/2; but the arm (with h1s2 at zero belief) reports no disbelief at all, and a refutation cannot flip a sign, so the report cannot show that the literature's sign would have made the MUC5B arm agree with its hypothesis.
render.py still accepts 'unsigned_association' as an unexpressed category although guide v2 turns those steps into assoc statements, so an un-upgraded curation passes the check silently.
